answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded random walks: each step mixes credibility only within a limited radius, so distant identities cannot instantly accumulate weight. A sybil cluster behaves like an isolated island in the atlas, connected to honest nodes by a sparse cut; its low conductance mathematically bounds escape probability and aggregate voting mass. Like a river crossing a narrow bridge, min-cut transitivity limits influence unless the cluster acquires proportionate honest attestations.
